subject: physics
question_text: Two springs of force constants k₁ and k₂ are connected in series and in parallel. Obtain the effective force constant in each case.

recall.must_convey: That in series the same force acts and the stretches add, giving one by k equals one by k one plus one by k two.

steps.label: Springs in parallel
lines: In PARALLEL both springs stretch by the SAME x,

lines.text: F = F₁ + F₂ = k₁x + k₂x = (k₁ + k₂)x

lines: Springs in parallel are stiffer, springs in
series are softer, than either one alone.
steps.why: Two springs side by side share the load, so the pair resists more than either alone — the stiffness simply adds.
common_mistakes: Using the reciprocal rule in parallel, which is the series rule.
Calling a mass held between two springs, one on each side, a series case — both springs push it back together, so k = k₁ + k₂ even though the springs lie in one line.

recall.must_convey: That in parallel the stretch is the same and the forces add, so k equals k one plus k two.
accept: k equals k one plus k two
